newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM PGM futures surge by price limits.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM PGM futures surge by price limits.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo platinum group metals (PGMs) ended sharply higher on Monday after surging by their daily price limits on short-covering backed by tight physical supplies, traders said.
All palladium futures, except the limitless spot August, jumped by their 36-yen limits. Benchmark June stood at 719 yen.

All platinum futures, except for the spot August, rose by their 50 yen per gram daily limit by the close. Benchmark June platinum ended at 1,544 yen. "Basically, there was little selling in the PGM market to counter active short-covering by private investors," one trader said.
Traders expected PGM prices to rise further, considering large TOCOM short positions in palladium.
"Unless private investors finish covering their massive short positions in TOCOM palladium, the upward trend will never come to an end," an official of a bullion house said.
Although Japan's physical platinum market has not been as tight as palladium, investors who could not buy palladium futures after prices hit limit-ups, bought platinum futures instead, they said.
Gold futures ended slightly lower, tracking weaker bullion prices, they said.
Gold futures ranged from four yen to nine yen per gram lower. Benchmark June gold was down six yen at 1,223 yen.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted weaker at $323.80/324.20 per ounce at 0752 GMT, against $324.40/90 in New York on Friday.

"In the bullion market, some selling, believed to have come from Australian producers dented spot gold prices in Asian hours," another trader said. In gold futures, price losses were partly offset by private investor bargain hunting, they said.
Silver futures were mixed after sluggish trade. Benchmark June silver was up 0.5 yen per 10 grams at 174.5 yen.
